summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of hypertension, atrial fibrillation, stroke, chronic constipation, and neuropathic pain was admitted for abdominal distension and hypotension. Initial imaging showed significant colonic dilation without obstruction. He developed fever and worsening distension, prompting empiric treatment for possible Clostridium difficile colitis and pneumonia. Antibiotics led to rapid improvement in symptoms and labs. Repeat imaging confirmed resolution of bowel dilation and no perforation. He resumed bowel movements, tolerated a pureed diet, and had stable vital signs. Pain was managed with gabapentin, morphine, and a lidocaine patch for foot pain. Iron supplementation was held due to possible infection. He was discharged to extended care on a 14-day course of oral vancomycin, finishing ciprofloxacin, Miralax, and with recommendations for swallow precautions, wound care, and outpatient colonoscopy.
